source.title: Semantic Subtyping: Challenges, Perspectives, and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: In semantic-subtyping-based systems such as the lambda-calculus system Duce and the pi-calculus system π, deciding subtyping appears to require deciding whether certain denotable types are atomic, or more generally whether a type contains finitely many atomic types that can be enumerated. What mathematical phenomenon makes atomic types arise so persistently in semantic subtyping, how tightly is the semantic-subtyping technique tied to decidability of atomicity, and is it reasonable and possible to study semantic-subtyping systems in which atomic types are not denotable and the subtype lattice is dense?

evidence.quote: Since these atomic types pop out so frequently a first challenge is understanding why this happens and therefore how much the semantic subtyping technique is tightened to the decidability of atomicity. In particular, we may wonder whether it is reasonable and possible to study systems in which atomic types are not denotable so that the set of subtypes of a type is dense.

accepted.question_text: For semantic subtyping enriched with polymorphic types, especially in the presence of contravariant type constructors such as arrow types and write-channel types, can one design a practical and semantically well-motivated polymorphism discipline? More specifically, can the marking approach to polymorphism be extended to contravariant constructors, can some of the original substitution-based polymorphic subtyping be recovered, and can one impose useful programming-language restrictions on polymorphic functions that keep the language both expressive and tractable?

evidence.quote: However, it is still matter of research how to implement the marking approach in the presence of contravariant type constructors: first and foremost in the presence of arrow types, as this would yield the definition of a polymorphic version of Duce; but also, it would be interesting to study the marking approach in the presence of the contravariant ch− type constructor, to check how it combines with the checks of atomicity required by the mix with the ch+ constructor, and see whether markings could suggests a solution to avoid this check of atomicity.

Finally, one can explore a more programming language oriented approach and check whether it is possible to define reasonable restrictions on the definition of polymorphic functions ... so that the resulting language provides the programmer with sufficient polymorphism for practical usage, while keeping it simple and manageable.

accepted.question_text: Is semantic subtyping merely an alternative semantic route to type systems that could in principle also be axiomatized syntactically, or does it fundamentally yield genuinely new classes of type systems? Equivalently, what are the real limits and degrees of freedom of the semantic-subtyping approach, and to what extent can the extensional interpretation underlying the models be systematized and characterized?
accepted.context_brief: Nature and limits of semantic subtyping

evidence.quote: As a matter of facts, we do not know whether the semantic subtyping approach is an innovative approach that yields to the definition of brand new type systems or it is just a new way to define old systems (or rather, systems that could be also defined in the good old syntactic way).
A more technical point is to investigate whether and to which extent it is possible to systematise the definition of the extensional interpretation.

accepted.question_text: When recursive types interact with channel or reference constructors in semantic subtyping, some natural recursive extensions appear to admit no model. What exactly does the non-existence of a model signify: a limitation of the semantic-subtyping methodology, or a deeper semantic obstruction inherent to those type constructors? More generally, can one characterize when recursive extensions of a semantically defined type system will or will not admit a model?

evidence.quote: This raises the problem to understand what the non-existence of a model means. Does it correspond to a limit of the semantic subtyping approach, a limit that some different approach could overcome, or does it instead characterise some mathematical properties of the semantics of the types, by reaching the limits that every semantic interpretation of these types cannot overcome?

accepted.question_text: How tightly is the semantic-subtyping approach tied to the presence of a type-case construct and explicit type annotations on values such as lambda-abstractions and channels? In particular, can semantic subtyping support useful languages without type-case, or any meaningful form of partial type reconstruction, while preserving the intended semantic distinctions and the model-based account of types?

evidence.quote: These observations make us wonder how much the semantic subtyping approach is bound to the presence of a type-case.

One may wonder if any form of partial type reconstruction is possible, and reformulate the previous question as whether the semantic subtyping approach is compatible with any form of type reconstruction.

accepted.question_text: For semantic-subtyping systems with negation types, especially systems like Duce and local variants of π where typing values may require infinitely many negated types or schematic representations, is the need for 'enough points' and explicit deduction of negated types an unavoidable feature of semantic subtyping, or can one recover simple minimum typing and a set-theoretic semantics without such infinitary or schematic machinery?

evidence.quote: So once more the question is whether this problem is a limitation of semantic subtyping or it is implicit in the usage of negation types. And as it can be 'solved' in the case case of π by considering the full system instead of just the local version, is it possible to find similar (and meaningful) solutions in other cases (notably for Duce)?

Finally, it would be interesting to check whether the semantic subtyping type system could be used to define a denotational semantics of the language by relating the semantic of an expression with the set of its types and (since our type system is closed by finite intersections and subsumption) build a filter model [BCD83].

accepted.question_text: What is the precise relationship between the semantic lambda-calculus system Duce and the local π-calculus system π? In particular, can one give a type-preserving encoding of Duce into π that preserves the subtyping relation and correctly handles overloaded functions, recursive types, and the channel type gap chλ(t) versus ch−(t), or do the obstacles encountered indicate a deeper mismatch that instead calls for an integrated concurrent version of Duce?

evidence.quote: There exist several encodings of the λ-calculus into the π-calculus ..., so it seems interesting to study whether the encoding of Duce into π is also possible.

Is this yet another characterisation of some limits of the approach? Does it just mean that Milner’s translation is unfit to model overloading? Or does it instead suggest that the encoding of Duce into π has not a lot of sense and that we had better study how to integrate Duce and π in order to define a concurrent version of Duce?

accepted.question_text: Can the semantic-subtyping methodology be extended fruitfully to dependent type systems, such as π-calculus systems with channel-dependent types or the first-order dependent type theory λΠ, in a way that yields a genuinely semantic characterization of subtyping rather than one tied primarily to syntactic normalization rules?

evidence.quote: As a final research direction for the semantic subtyping we want to hint at the research on dependent types.
It would then be interesting to check whether the semantic subtyping approach yields a more semantic characterisation of the subtyping relation for dependent types.
